newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes led down by weak wet and paper Brent.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes led down by weak wet and paper Brent.

text.p: North Sea crude markets weakened on Monday after a prompt wet Brent cargo was sold some 20 cents lower than a physical Brent deal struck earlier in the day, and paper Brent values slumped.
The cargo loading Jan 18-20 fetched just Feb Brent -30 cents, after a Jan 25-27 loader was earlier traded at Feb Brent -10 cents.
Although the later deal was for a prompt cargo, traders said it signalled a weakening in values for third decade cargoes.
"The market (for third decade Brents) is certainly under (Feb Brent) -10 cents now, probably more around -20," one said.

A seller offering a Jan 25-27 Brent at Feb Brent -5 cents found no takers. Despite the bearish sentiment, the two Brent dates nominated from the paper chains were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
Traders said that a pick up in transatlantic trade was needed to put a floor under prices.
The U.S. arbitrage remained open although traders struggled to place cargoes on the U.S. Gulf Coast due to sickly margins and the approach of spring refinery maintenance.
Other North Sea grades were also seen under pressure, with a Jan 26-28 Statfjord trading weaker at Dated Brent +32 cents.
But the sale by a major Norwegian producer of two million barrels of late January-loading Oseberg to the Far East should help ease a potential end-January overhang, traders said.
On the paper market, outright Brent values slumped, with Feb paper trading a hefty 68 cents down at $23.66 a barrel at 1854 GMT as U.S. products futures crashed.
Cfds were slow to fall in line with weakening values for physical Brent. This week's dates traded at Feb Brent -10 cents, while Jan 20-24 traded at Mar Brent +34 cents.
Brent intermonth spreads eased lower, with Feb/Mar traded at +45 and +44 cents and Mar/Apr at +50 cents.
